title: Beresford Drive Play Park
description:
The play park at Beresford Drive in Melton was divested to the Parish Council in April 2021 from East Suffolk District Council. This is one of three play parks in the village that the Parish Council owns. The main play park is at the Recreation Ground on Melton Road.

In 2022 the swings had to be removed after the annual inspection as the structure was deemed unsafe. The Parish Council identified the park as an area that needed investment and was made a priority project for the 2023/24 financial year. A public consultation was carried out in Spring 2023 in the form of a survey and open afternoon.

The consultation demonstrated that there is a need for this playpark and that it requires a full refurbishment. The overall response was a desire to revamp the play area to make it a space that people are proud of, want to visit and provides imaginative play and equipment for all ages. There were some concerns about older children hanging out and intimidating younger children and the area being used for illegal activities. It is important that the layout and equipment should be mindful of these concerns.
https://melton-suffolk-pc.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/MPC_23_84.02Beresford_Drive.pdf

The Brief
Design and install a new play park at Beresford Drive that caters for a wide range of ages and is inclusive and accessible. It is expected that all existing equipment will be unsuitable for re-use and will need to be removed and disposed of.

Ideally the fencing should not be moved although if extending the play area slightly would result in a better configuration this could be considered. The gates will probably need to be replaced. Some equipment could be placed outside of the fenced area if deemed appropriate.

Play equipment should cater for a wide range of ages eg 0-3 (toddler), 3-12 (children), 10-20 (youth) and multigenerational (0-99).

The most requested equipment identified in the consultation: Slide, Swings, Roundabout, Climbing Frame, benches/picnic benches and basketball hoop.

Consideration must be given to safety and anti-social behaviour concerns.

The equipment should be easy to maintain, incur low maintenance costs and be robust.

Budget
The Council has some reserves set aside and will be seeking match funding grants to cover the full costs. We welcome a variety of designs/options with a budget ranging from £20k to £80k.

Timelines
Designs and quotes should be sent by email to the Parish Council by the 10th October 2023. Site visits can be arranged.

title: Monitoring and Evaluation of North & East Melton Mowbray Distributor Road Construction
description:
Monitoring and Evaluation Consultancy

Leicestershire County Council invites bids for the provision of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) services for a major scheme in line with the Department for Transport's (DfT) Enhanced Monitoring requirements. This tender will evaluate the implementation, outcomes, and impacts of the scheme, ensuring accountability for public investment and assessing whether the scheme meets its objectives.

The consultancy package consists of three key stages:

1. Baseline & Pre-Construction Assessment: Review existing data, perform gap analysis, and prepare a Baseline Report.

2. 1-Year Post-Opening Assessment: Data collection, impact evaluation, and production of the 1-Year Report.

3. 5-Year Post-Opening Assessment: Data collection, impact evaluation, and production of the 5-Year Report.

Key Objectives:

Assess whether the scheme's objectives, including reductions in traffic congestion, carbon emissions, noise, and improved air quality, have been met.

Evaluate travel demand, public transport use, active travel modes, and economic impacts.

Conduct process, impact, and economic evaluations to measure the scheme's outcomes and unintended impacts.

Timescales:
This contract spans all three stages, with deliverables scheduled at Baseline, 1 Year Post-Opening, and 5 Years Post-Opening.

Additional Details:
Pre-scheme traffic data has been collected (March 2023), but further analysis and reporting are required as part of this tender.

description:
Provide Melton Borough with an updated Playing Pitch Strategy (PPS) and Indoor Sports Facilities Strategy (ISFS) and will do this by providing the following deliverables: 
Playing Pitch Strategy
•	Stage A report that sets out, for example, the scope of the study, sub-area analysis and timescales (electronic pdf)
•	Stage B summary report outlining the supply/demand data capture during the consultation and auditing stage (electronic pdf)
•	An updated PPS database of audit and demand information (excel sheet)
•	A Full GIS dataset (point data) linked to the PPS database - maps are provided on a sport-by-sport basis in each assessment report and electronically as part of the GIS data
•	Full PPS database training for officer(s) responsible for maintaining the database.
•	Assessment report on a sport-by-sport basis focusing on reporting research findings, consultation, site audit information and data analysis supported by detailed GIS mapping (electronic pdf)
•	A Playing Pitch Strategy - including a review of existing/advice on proposed, planning policy recommendations, appropriate responses and establishing approaches to secure developer contributions (electronic pdf)
•	A site by site, area by area action plans addressing key issues identified in the assessment reports. They provide recommendations based on current usage levels, quality and future demand, as well as site potential for enhancement (electronic pdf)
•	A Populated Playing Pitch Calculator with three housing growth scenarios and a KKP Toolkit guide and easy-to-use step by step approach for use by planners
Indoor and Built Facilities Strategy
•	A multi-layer ISFS database in Excel within which enables storage of supply and demand information.  
•	GIS MapInfo (compatible with all GIS packages) linking to the database and is designed for council use. 
•	An assessment report identifying key area characteristics, findings and issues. Which meets the requirements the NPFF, providing a robust, up to date assessment of need. It covers facility quality, quantity, accessibility and availability.
•	An Indoor Sports Facilities Strategy and Action Plan - a series of recommendations to ensure that the correct facilities are available to meet identified deficiencies, future need and/or specific NGB, the Council and/or major stakeholder aspirations
•	Provide support, tools and guidance on Sports Facilities Calculator

title: FEW1333 - Home Care Services Leicester
description:
The current Home Care Framework (currently named the Domiciliary Support Service) is due to expire on 6th October 2024 with procurement planned for October/November 2023. The contract had the option to extend for up to two years, and these have been utilised. The current jointly commissioned Framework began on 9th October 2017 and is supported by the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland NHS Integrated Care Board. A commissioning review has been undertaken to re-procure this statutory provision. A multi-disciplinary programme board has overseen the review arrangements which are led by senior officers in the ASC strategic commissioning team. Members include representatives from the Integrated Care Board and NHS Midlands & Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit.

The tender opportunity for the provision of ASC0288 - Home Care Service was advertised on 15th November 2023. The deadline for submissions was 2pm on Tuesday 19th December 2023. In February 2024, due to reasons beyond the Council's control and in line with section 4.22.10 of the ITT (Part One) document, the decision was made to abort the current procurement process ASC0288 - Home Care Service Leicester. A final award will therefore not be made, and the procurement process has been terminated. 

A new procurement exercise for homecare services went live on 26th February 2024. The indicative timeline indicates that contract award won't take place until September/October 2024, which does not leave enough time to mobilise contracts, before the existing contracts expire on 6th October 2024. This is a statutory service, and the waiver is required to bridge the gap between the current contracts ending and the new arrangements being in place after a compliant procurement exercise.

title: Provision of Leicestershire Holiday Activities and Food Programme - Holiday Clubs
description:
Leicestershire County Council (the Council) is conducting a procurement to establish a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) in accordance with the Light-Touch Regime requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.\r
\r
The Council is inviting Providers to join the Leicestershire Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) Programme DPS to supply holiday club places to children resident in Leicestershire who are eligible to receive benefits-related free school meals. HAF holiday provision is for school aged children from reception to year 11 (inclusive).\r
\r
The offer of free HAF holiday club provision will be available to all Leicestershire children in receipt of benefits-related free school meals. However, it is not expected that all eligible children will take up the offer of HAF holiday club places as attendance is voluntary.\r
\r
We are seeking provision to be delivered across the County and particularly targeting areas of greatest need. The holiday clubs will take place during the Easter, Summer and Christmas school holidays.\r
\r
Holiday club provision must provide each child with; a healthy meal; engaging and enriching activities; opportunities to be physically active; nutritional education. Provision must also ensure that each child's family develop their understanding of health and nutrition, and are signposted towards other information and support, for example, health, employment, and education.\r
\r
The DPS will run for an in initial period of 2 years and 2 months from 1st November 2022 with the potential to extend in yearly increments for up to three years.\r
\r
Providers can submit an application to join the DPS at any time during the life of the DPS. The deadline for receipt of applications for Round 1 of the DPS is 12:00 12th September 2022. Once a DPS round is closed, the next round will automatically open to receive further applications until the end of the DPS.\r
